qAndA.question: What type of molecules are depicted in purple within the cell membrane?

qAndA.answer: They form a two-layer framework called a phospholipid bilayer.

qAndA.answer: It provides an interactive labeling exercise that reinforces the viewer's understanding of the cell membrane structure by prompting them to actively recall and apply the information presented in the first scene.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: A cell is separated from its environment by a selectively permeable plasma membrane.
The plasma membrane is commonly described as a fluid mosaic.
It is like a mosaic and having diverse protein molecules embedded in a matrix of phospholipids.
Its component proteins and phospholipid molecules can move about, so it is quite fluid and flexible.
The phospholipids in a membrane form a two-layer framework called a phospholipid bilayer.
The steroid cholesterol helps stabilize the phospholipids.
Carpohydrate molecules are attached to some of the molecules that make up the membrane.
